query: Which material can be used for lightweight and superior comprehensive performance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA alloy exhibits superior comprehensive performance due to its homogeneous microstructure and balanced properties, which can be attributed to the eutectic design strategy utilizing physicochemical properties and CALPHAD thermodynamics calculations.
generation.intervention: Eutectic design strategy and CALPHAD thermodynamics calculations
generation.conditions: Alloy design and thermodynamic calculation phase
generation.mechanism: Eutectic design strategy utilizing physicochemical properties (atomic radius, mixing enthalpy, valence electron concentration) and CALPHAD thermodynamics calculations
generation.boundary: Requires reliable thermodynamics databases for HEAs to be established
generation.uncertainty: Assumption of a pseudo-binary multi-component alloy system

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA alloy designed using eutectic design strategy with alloy designed using traditional physical metallurgy principles
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy designed using traditional physical metallurgy principles exhibits similar or superior comprehensive performance, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: The eutectic design strategy utilizes physicochemical properties (atomic radius, mixing enthalpy, valence electron concentration) and CALPHAD thermodynamics calculations to pinpoint eutectic compositions in multi-component systems.. System: General class of Eutectic High-Entropy Alloys (EHEAs). Conditions: Alloy design and thermodynamic calculation phase. Evidence: inferred. Observation: The authors successfully designed the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 alloy using this strategy, resulting in a uniform microstructure and balanced properties.. Scope limits: Requires reliable thermodynamics databases for HEAs to be established; relies on the assumption of a pseudo-binary multi-component alloy system.. Alternatives: Traditional physical metallurgy principles which may not easily predict eutectic behavior in high-entropy systems.. Quote: "Further exploration of new EHEAs will be based on previous established physical metallurgy principles to design HEAs, utilizing physiochemical material properties including atomic radius, mixing enthalpy and valence electron concentration."
